Interview Experience
Pranav Shukla
Computer Engineering

Offline Presentation (About the Company)
National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is a digital payments
powerhouse, renowned for creating UPI and Fastag. Handling 80% of the
country's transactions, NPCI is a vital contributor to India's economy,
constituting 5% of the GDP. Beyond India, they aim to extend UPI's
dominance globally, reaching Africa and South American countries.
Crucially, NPCI, despite being government founded, operates as a non-profit
organization. The Unified Payment Interface (UPI) is a testament to their
innovation, facilitating 9.3 billion transactions and 6.2 billion API hits daily.
Involved in diverse projects like metrocard development, NPCI explores
future prospects in blockchain, cloud computing, no-code computing, trust
architecture, IoT, and 5G transactions.
NPCI aspires to be the Google of the world, addressing cyber threats and
fraud challenges through robust security measures, including AI and ML.
With a lower fraud rate compared to Visa, they constantly innovate,
launching six products, such as UPI Lite for internet-less peer-to-peer
payments and a voice-based payment feature for BHIM.
Differentiating itself with inclusivity, NPCI offers certification programs,
mandatory training, and champions diversity and inclusion. Operating with a
startup mindset, they conduct internal hackathons and maintain a
cutting-edge transaction speed of 500 milliseconds. NPCI fosters an
environment for aspiring developers, emphasizing full-stack development
and openness to learning new technologies. More than a
government-funded startup, NPCI is a visionary force shaping the future of
digital payments.
1

Selection Process
NPCI visited VJTI for the first time. (Because I couldn't find any interview
experience online, I'm confident it was their first year of on-campus hiring.)
Eligibility Criteria:
1. 10th/ SSC - 60 % and above
2. 12th / HSC/ Diploma - 60 % and above
3. BE/BTECH - 60 % and above (Till current Sem)
4. No live backlog
5. Only 1 year gap between 12th & BE/BTech
Stipend: 30,000/pm
Role and location of internship were not mentioned.
Assessment Pattern
1. Online Assessment:
Section A – Verbal ability, logical reasoning, and quants.Basic aptitude
questions , but there was a strict time constraint.
Section B – Machine learning 20 questions. This was unexpected as they
didn't mention what all to expect in the online assessment , this happens a
lot , some companies may include web development questions too. I
fortunately had revised ML since they had mentioned in their ppt that they
want students who are interested to work on ML, data science and
blockchain.
Section C – Essay on random topic, 224 word limit. Didn't expect this in the
test, but not an issue. I included a lot of keywords in this essay.
Section D – Coding, 2 questions of easy to medium difficulty.
The 1st question was a variation of the rat in a maze problem.
The 2nd question was that, given an array of N numbers. Each time the
minimum number in the array is selected, its adjacent elements and the
member itself are deleted and this happens till no numbers are left in the
2

array. We were supposed to find the total of the minimum numbers being
deleted. Similar question: Minimum number.
15 out of 180 students were shortlisted for the interviews.
Technical Interview:
Prepare well for an interview, ensure that you are well-acquainted with the
content on your resume, thoroughly. I thought it was an easy thing and
started preparing for it pretty late which took a big chunk of my preparation
time. Avoid that. I prepared the tech stack which I had mentioned and any
cross question /HR question on my background, achievements and
experiences.
Also my seniors had their NPCI placement interview just a day before my
interview so I asked many of them about their interview experiences.
Surprisingly they were asked mostly about their projects and hard questions
on CS fundamentals and not a single coding question which most people
fear. I was super happy , I prepared CS fundamentals properly and was
ready to give a crisp summary of my projects , but of course that didn't
happen.
I was first asked to give my introduction , and right after that one of the
panel members asked me which language I am comfortable in ( I said C++).
After which he asked me these questions:
1. Difference between C and C++
2. What data structures do you know?
3. Explain Linked list and Arrays.
After this he asked me to screenshare and to print the first 3 elements of an
array and then print the reverse . The question was easy and I did it in a few
minutes. The only problem was that I was using an online compiler which
was lagging while I printed the output. I was asking him simple questions
like should i put in dummy values for the array, just to make sure . I
apologized when my compiler was lagging but the panel member said "don't
give excuses , it may be your compiler's issue or your network issue.” His
remarks were a bit surprising because I had coded this easy question in a
3

minute! But then I remembered that interviewers do this purposely just to
check if the candidate maintains his cool or his attitude changes drastically.
My friends who got an internship in Citibank had faced such interviewers
during their Hr round, where the interviewers were sweet but they asked
questions in a tricky manner.
So after my code was run properly he gave his approval and the next
panelist started asking questions.
He asked me how to detect a loop in a linked list. I asked him some
questions to understand the question properly and then gave him the
answer. He approved right away!
Some more questions that were asked to friends during the interview are:
Find if the number is prime or not, find sum of unique elements in the array,
Implement doubly linked list first from a given array, find the second highest
element in an array without using inbuilt sorting function.
Moving on, the next panelist of my interview was ready to ask questions but
due to some net issue he left the meeting , so I wasn't asked any CS
fundamental questions. After which the last panelist asked me if I was
interested in ML or data science. I shared my interest in ML and told him
about the two web+ML projects nn my resume in brief. Then they asked if I
had any questions , so I asked what tech stacks and what projects I would
work on ? The interview was then concluded. Only 1 round of interview was
conducted.
12 students were selected for the internship.
4

Resources and Tips:
DSA: It is important for your online assessment tests as well as your
interview rounds. Try to not get confused with plenty of resources available
on the internet. I followed these resources:
1. Leetcode Blind 75
2. Striver SDE Sheet or DSA Sheet by Love Babbar
CS Fundamentals: Some companies ask questions from these topics in their
assessment rounds in MCQ Format. Mainly questions are asked in interview
rounds from this topic. It includes Computer Science core subjects like
Operating Systems, OOPS, Data Structures and Algorithms (theory), DBMS,
CN(not important for internships) - basics only .
1. Follow Interviewbit sheets which are easily available online
2. If you want video content you can follow either gate smashers or love
babbar, they have playlists on each subject.
Aptitude: For this try to solve some questions in your free time.
These resources are exactly what my senior recommended and I have
followed it.
TIPS:
1. In your assessments, for MCQ rounds try to be as fast as possible
when there is no negative marking.
2. For coding questions, try to start by taking a look at all the questions
and then solve with a basic approach if you don’t have any idea of
how to solve a question.
3. In technical interviews, take your time to explain questions asked.
Never get puzzled in your words. Think before speaking and while
explaining.
4. Be prepared with your projects and questions like: your motivation
behind
5. creating those, tech stack used by you, why that tech stack, etc.
5

6. Read company archives as companies repeat questions and have a
specific pattern of hiring.
7. Give mock interviews to your friends or seniors (they are there for
you).
8. Try to take advice from seniors, they are always ready to help
whenever you need.
9. Don't lose hope.
Because my pointer wasn't very good, I had to take advantage of every
opportunity I got. It gets stressful when u dont get an internship after a
handful of companies have gone by. I was lucky enough to get an internship
after 5 companies, but that isn't the case for everyone. The only thing that is
in your control and the only thing u should focus on is that u have prepared
well and you are giving your best. At the same time you are correcting your
mistakes and continuously improving yourself. It does get stressful if u dont
get an internship for a long time or if u dont get an internship at all, but it's
ok , you will definitely do good in the long run. Don't give up.
Feel free to contact me- PranavShukla
